newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Dissidents still control Lesotho police command.
newsitem.headline: Dissidents still control Lesotho police command.

text.p: The Lesotho police headquarters in Maseru was still under siege on Saturday by eight members of the Royal Lesotho Mounted Police, despite negotiations with the government and church leaders, state radio reported.

A government statement said the eight -- who are resisting arrest over the killing of three fellow officers in October 1995 -- had "attempted to relieve a number of senior officers of their duties" since taking over the station on Thursday.
Radio quoted the dissidents as saying they had rounded up the senior officers, including the acting police commissioner, and dismissed them.

The mutineers said they would also sack the police commissioner of the tiny landlocked mountain kingdom when he returned from Namibia, where he is attending a Southern African Development Community conference.
The dissident officers are claiming amnesty under Lesotho's Pardons Act, which stipulates that security force members may not be charged for any crimes committed from 1993 to 1995.
"This illegal action appears to have been taken as an attempt to further delay the appearance of the suspected officers in court," the statement said.

Local news reports said the officers were also retaliating for the alleged killing of a junior policeman who had supported their refusal to stand trial. He was gunned down at his Maseru home last weekend.
